questions.question: What is the single best thing you can do to survive an accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when you ride?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Use a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside a vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver cannot see you. It also blocks your escape route if another hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you remember about motorcycle blind spots in traffic?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are too small to cause problems.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever is comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely for proper protection.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride their motorcycle?

options.text: Tell them to take quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Do whatever you can to stop them, including taking their keys. Find them another way to get home.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires before riding?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check the air pressure, tread, and general wear of your tires. Shininess is not important.

questions.question: Which material offers the best protection for motorcycle clothing?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcyclists. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal covers are all hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: Regular maintenance on your motorcycle helps because:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance and inspections are important parts of keeping your motorcycle in good condition.

questions.question: Which color should you wear to be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green make you easier to see while riding. Wear bright clothing any time of day you ride.

questions.question: Mirror checks should:

options.text: Only be done on long trips.
Be part of your regular scanning routine.
Not be done because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Always use your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.

questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your riding ability.

questions.question: To get the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely and allow them to get in front of you. Riding faster may increase danger.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. These signs tell you about road rules. You must follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to improve your grip on the handgrips.
Not be worn because they make it harder to use the controls.
Only be worn on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to improve your grip on the handgrips.
questions.explanation: Wear leather or other durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handgrips and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no other drivers are nearby.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do about lane position?

options.text: Stay in the same part of the lane all the time.
Weave back and forth to keep other drivers out.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No one lane position is always best. Move your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before every ride?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check the spokes for bending or damage, tire tread condition, and all lights. The seat fabric does not affect safety.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.
